A fixed calibrated unitary cannot map arbitrary input superpositions to one of their calibrated outcome branches; this linearity result does not forbid a unitary rotation of one particular known state. The framework therefore separates quantum multiplicity from classical actuality. The global state and its unitary dynamics represent quantum physical structure, while classical outcomes are stable equivalence classes of fine histories defined by an effectively commutative macroscopic record algebra. For decoherent history bundles, squared Hilbert-space norm is characterized as the unique normalized, continuous, unitarily invariant, and orthogonally additive branch weight.
